captures.stdout:
A client to manage innernet network interfaces.

Usage: innernet [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  install                 Install a new innernet config
  show                    Enumerate all innernet connections
  up                      Bring up your local interface, and update it with latest peer list
  fetch                   Fetch and update your local interface with the latest peer list
  uninstall               Uninstall an innernet network
  down                    Bring down the interface (equivalent to 'wg-quick down INTERFACE')
  add-peer                Add a new peer
  rename-peer             Rename a peer
  add-cidr                Add a new CIDR
  rename-cidr             Rename a CIDR
  delete-cidr             Delete a CIDR
  list-cidrs              List CIDRs
  disable-peer            Disable an enabled peer
  enable-peer             Enable a disabled peer
  add-association         Add an association between CIDRs
  delete-association      Delete an association between CIDRs
  list-associations       List existing assocations between CIDRs
  set-listen-port         Set the local listen port
  override-endpoint       Override your external endpoint that the server sends to other peers
  override-peer-endpoint  Override the endpoint you use to connect to a particular peer
  completions             Generate shell completion scripts
  help                    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...               Verbose output, use -vv for even higher verbositude
  -c, --config-dir <CONFIG_DIR>  [default: /etc/innernet]
  -d, --data-dir <DATA_DIR>      [default: /var/lib/innernet]
      --no-routing               Whether the routing should be done by innernet or is done by an
                                 external tool like e.g. babeld
      --backend <BACKEND>        Specify a WireGuard backend to use. If not set, innernet will
                                 auto-select based on availability [default: kernel] [possible
                                 values: kernel, userspace]
      --mtu <MTU>                Specify the desired MTU for your interface (default: 1280)
  -h, --help                     Print help
  -V, --version                  Print version

Install a new innernet config

Usage: innernet install [OPTIONS] <INVITE>

Arguments:
  <INVITE>  Path to the invitation file

Options:
      --listen-port <LISTEN_PORT>
          The local WireGuard listen port
      --hosts-path <HOSTS_PATH>
          The path to write hosts to [default: /etc/hosts]
      --no-write-hosts
          Don't write to any hosts files
      --host-suffix <HOST_SUFFIX>
          Use a different suffix for hosts, than 'INTERFACE.wg' , ex. --host-suffix 'evilnet' names
          peers: PEER.evilnet, and --host-suffix '' gives peers no suffix, just: PEER
      --name <NAME>
          Set a specific interface name
      --default-name
          Use the network name inside the invitation as the interface name
  -d, --delete-invite
          Delete the invitation after a successful install
      --no-nat-traversal
          Don't attempt NAT traversal. Note that this still will report candidates unless you also
          specify to exclude all NAT candidates
      --exclude-nat-candidates <EXCLUDE_NAT_CANDIDATES>
          Exclude one or more CIDRs from NAT candidate reporting. ex. --exclude-nat-candidates
          '0.0.0.0/0' would report no candidates
      --no-nat-candidates
          Don't report any candidates to coordinating server. Shorthand for --exclude-nat-candidates
          '0.0.0.0/0'
  -h, --help
          Print help

Enumerate all innernet connections

Usage: innernet show [OPTIONS] [INTERFACE]

Arguments:
  [INTERFACE]  

Options:
  -s, --short  One-line peer list
  -t, --tree   Display peers in a tree based on the CIDRs
  -h, --help   Print help

Bring up your local interface, and update it with latest peer list

Usage: innernet up [OPTIONS] [INTERFACE]

Arguments:
  [INTERFACE]  

Options:
  -d, --daemon
          Enable daemon mode i.e. keep the process running, while fetching the latest peer list
          periodically
      --interval <INTERVAL>
          Keep fetching the latest peer list at the specified interval in seconds. Valid only in
          daemon mode [default: 60]
      --hosts-path <HOSTS_PATH>
          The path to write hosts to [default: /etc/hosts]
      --no-write-hosts
          Don't write to any hosts files
      --host-suffix <HOST_SUFFIX>
          Use a different suffix for hosts, than 'INTERFACE.wg' , ex. --host-suffix 'evilnet' names
          peers: PEER.evilnet, and --host-suffix '' gives peers no suffix, just: PEER
      --no-nat-traversal
          Don't attempt NAT traversal. Note that this still will report candidates unless you also
          specify to exclude all NAT candidates
      --exclude-nat-candidates <EXCLUDE_NAT_CANDIDATES>
          Exclude one or more CIDRs from NAT candidate reporting. ex. --exclude-nat-candidates
          '0.0.0.0/0' would report no candidates
      --no-nat-candidates
          Don't report any candidates to coordinating server. Shorthand for --exclude-nat-candidates
          '0.0.0.0/0'
  -h, --help
          Print help

Fetch and update your local interface with the latest peer list

Usage: innernet fetch [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --hosts-path <HOSTS_PATH>
          The path to write hosts to [default: /etc/hosts]
      --no-write-hosts
          Don't write to any hosts files
      --host-suffix <HOST_SUFFIX>
          Use a different suffix for hosts, than 'INTERFACE.wg' , ex. --host-suffix 'evilnet' names
          peers: PEER.evilnet, and --host-suffix '' gives peers no suffix, just: PEER
      --no-nat-traversal
          Don't attempt NAT traversal. Note that this still will report candidates unless you also
          specify to exclude all NAT candidates
      --exclude-nat-candidates <EXCLUDE_NAT_CANDIDATES>
          Exclude one or more CIDRs from NAT candidate reporting. ex. --exclude-nat-candidates
          '0.0.0.0/0' would report no candidates
      --no-nat-candidates
          Don't report any candidates to coordinating server. Shorthand for --exclude-nat-candidates
          '0.0.0.0/0'
  -h, --help
          Print help

Uninstall an innernet network

Usage: innernet uninstall [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --yes   Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help  Print help

Bring down the interface (equivalent to 'wg-quick down INTERFACE')

Usage: innernet down <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Add a new peer

By default, you'll be prompted interactively to create a peer, but you can also specify all the
options in the command, eg:

--name 'person' --cidr 'humans' --admin false --auto-ip --save-config 'person.toml' --yes

Usage: innernet add-peer [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>
          

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Name of new peer

      --ip <IP>
          Specify desired IP of new peer (within parent CIDR)

      --auto-ip
          Auto-assign the peer the first available IP within the CIDR

      --cidr <CIDR>
          Name of CIDR to add new peer under

      --admin <ADMIN>
          Make new peer an admin?
          
          [possible values: true, false]

      --yes
          Bypass confirmation

      --save-config <SAVE_CONFIG>
          Save the config to the given location

      --invite-expires <INVITE_EXPIRES>
          Invite expiration period (eg. '30d', '7w', '2h', '60m', '1000s')

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Rename a peer

By default, you'll be prompted interactively to select a peer, but you can also specify all the
options in the command, eg:

--name 'person' --new-name 'human'

Usage: innernet rename-peer [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>
          

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Name of peer to rename

      --new-name <NEW_NAME>
          The new name of the peer

      --yes
          Bypass confirmation

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Add a new CIDR

Usage: innernet add-cidr [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --name <NAME>      The CIDR name (eg. 'engineers')
      --cidr <CIDR>      The CIDR network (eg. '10.42.5.0/24')
      --parent <PARENT>  The CIDR parent name
      --yes              Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help             Print help

Rename a CIDR

By default, you'll be prompted interactively to select a CIDR, but you can also specify all the
options in the command, eg:

--name 'group' --new-name 'family'

Usage: innernet rename-cidr [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>
          

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Name of CIDR to rename

      --new-name <NEW_NAME>
          The new name of the CIDR

      --yes
          Bypass confirmation

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Delete a CIDR

Usage: innernet delete-cidr [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --name <NAME>  The CIDR name (eg. 'engineers')
      --yes          Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help         Print help

List CIDRs

Usage: innernet list-cidrs [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
  -t, --tree  Display CIDRs in tree format
  -h, --help  Print help

Disable an enabled peer

Usage: innernet disable-peer [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --name <NAME>  Name of peer to enable/disable
      --yes          Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help         Print help

Enable a disabled peer

Usage: innernet enable-peer [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --name <NAME>  Name of peer to enable/disable
      --yes          Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help         Print help

Add an association between CIDRs

Usage: innernet add-association [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE> [CIDR1] [CIDR2]

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  
  [CIDR1]      The first cidr to associate
  [CIDR2]      The second cidr to associate

Options:
      --yes   Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help  Print help

Delete an association between CIDRs

Usage: innernet delete-association [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE> [CIDR1] [CIDR2]

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  
  [CIDR1]      The first cidr to associate
  [CIDR2]      The second cidr to associate

Options:
      --yes   Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help  Print help

List existing assocations between CIDRs

Usage: innernet list-associations <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Set the local listen port

Usage: innernet set-listen-port [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
  -l, --listen-port <LISTEN_PORT>  The listen port you'd like to set for the interface
  -u, --unset                      Unset the local listen port to use a randomized port
      --yes                        Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help                       Print help

Override your external endpoint that the server sends to other peers

Usage: innernet override-endpoint [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
  -e, --endpoint <ENDPOINT>  The external endpoint that you'd like the innernet server to broadcast
                             to other peers. The IP address may be unspecified (all zeros), in which
                             case the server will try to resolve it based on its most recent
                             connection. The port will still be used, even if you decide to use an
                             unspecified IP address
  -u, --unset                Unset an existing override to use the automatic endpoint discovery
      --yes                  Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help                 Print help

Override the endpoint you use to connect to a particular peer

Usage: innernet override-peer-endpoint [OPTIONS] <INTERFACE>

Arguments:
  <INTERFACE>  

Options:
      --name <NAME>          Name of peer whose endpoint you want to override
  -e, --endpoint <ENDPOINT>  The external endpoint that you'd like to use for a given peer
  -u, --unset                Unset an existing local endpoint override for this peer
      --yes                  Bypass confirmation
  -h, --help                 Print help

Generate shell completion scripts

Usage: innernet completions <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>  [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
